h: Bounce first, then ride the Metro to the coast
p: A session on giant inflatables is a short, intense blast, so think of it as the warm-up act for a bigger Tyneside day. Plan to arrive early, because getting a group of excited kids into socks, out of coats and lined up for the safety talk always takes longer than you think. If you've got a mix of ages, have a quiet word with the older ones about giving the little ones a bit of room on the busier sections; it keeps everyone smiling.

Afterwards, Newcastle's museums are a gift for families. The Discovery Museum tells the story of Tyneside's inventors and shipbuilders and is home to Turbinia, once the fastest ship in the world, which takes up a whole hall. The Great North Museum: Hancock has dinosaurs, Egyptian mummies and a planetarium, and it's handy for the city centre. The Life Science Centre near Central Station is a hands-on science attraction that's ideal for curious minds.

If the sun's out, the Tyne and Wear Metro can whisk you to the coast in no time. Tynemouth has a sandy beach, a castle and priory ruins on the headland, and a popular weekend market in the old station. Whitley Bay, a few stops along, has a long beach and the white dome of Spanish City overlooking the seafront. Over in Gateshead, the Angel of the North is worth a quick stop for a photo on your way in or out, and the Baltic arts centre on the riverside is free to visit.
